newsitem.title: USA: Conoco rejects green group's Utah land swap.
newsitem.headline: Conoco rejects green group's Utah land swap.

text.p: Conoco Inc rejected an effort by green groups to stop it from drilling for oil on leases it holds in a national monument in Utah, an official with the Southern Utah Wilderness Alliance said Monday.

At a meeting last Friday with officials from Conoco, a subsidiary of DuPont Co, four environmental groups proposed a land swap to get Conoco to give up state and federal oil leases in the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument, created last year by President Bill Clinton.
"We were not able to work things out," said Scott Groene, issues director for the southern Utah alliance.
"We were offering to work with them on how we could get them out of the national monument and satisfy their needs," he said.
Conoco officials said they could not swap the land without knowing how much it was worth, and that would first require exploratory drilling, the groups and a Conoco spokesman said.
"We said we don't really understand how you can establish a value for our leases without having drilled them," said Conoco spokesman Carlton Adams.
The company applied last month to drill for oil on a state lease and a federal lease in the monument area. When Clinton named it a monument, he said existing leases would be honored.
Conoco estimates that the area could hold more than a hundred million barrels of oil reserves. It has been considering drilling on the property over the last two years.
